version: 2
models:
- name: dim_date
  description: One row per UTC day from 2025-10-01 to 2026-12-31, placed relative to that year's release Thursday.
  config:
    meta:
      dex:
        grain:
          - date_day
        population:
          rule: Every calendar day in the spine; 2025 days belong to the control year (anchor Thu 20 Nov 2025), 2026 days to the study (anchor Thu 19 Nov 2026).
        assumptions:
          - decision: Control anchor
            chosen: Thu 20 Nov 2025 vs Thu 13 Nov 2025
            evidence: request
            detail: same week of November, one year earlier, both a week before US Thanksgiving week
          - decision: Thursday comparison roles
            chosen: removed
            evidence: request
            detail: they tagged the old index's release and baseline Thursdays
            column: comparison_role
  columns:
  - name: date_day
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: key
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - unique
    - not_null
  - name: study_year
    description: 2026 = GTA 6 release year; 2025 = seasonality control.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: release_day
    description: That year's anchor Thursday.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: attribute
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: days_from_release
    description: 0 on that year's anchor Thursday.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
          unit: days
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: iso_day_of_week
    description: 1 = Monday ... 7 = Sunday.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: day_name
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: attribute
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: is_gta_release_day
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null

version: 2
models:
- name: fct_signal_daily
  description: One row per signal per UTC day inside the study and control windows, with its place relative to release.
  config:
    meta:
      dex:
        grain:
          - signal_day_key
        population:
          rule: Signal-days whose date falls in dim_date; days outside the spine are dropped by the inner join.
        assumptions:
          - decision: Days outside the window
            chosen: dropped
            evidence: request
            detail: the study compares Thursdays in Oct-Nov 2026 against the same weeks of 2025; the inner join to dim_date keeps only that spine
            column: signal_date
          - decision: Surrogate key
            chosen: md5 of the natural grain
            evidence: default
            detail: the key is md5 of the composite Dex drafts as the grain, so the two describe the same rows; MetricFlow needs a single-column primary entity
          - decision: Thursday comparison roles
            chosen: removed
            evidence: request
            detail: they tagged the old index's release and baseline Thursdays
            column: comparison_role
          - decision: Google Trends rows and comparison roles
            chosen: removed
            evidence: request
            detail: 'user: scratch the old Day-Off Index; Trends moved to the new index'
            column: source
  columns:
  - name: source
    description: bluesky, reddit, hacker_news or wikipedia.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: signal
    description: What is counted, e.g. posts:day_off, posts:day_off_gta, pageviews:grand_theft_auto_vi.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: signal_family
    description: day_off_intent (people saying or searching they are off), day_off_gta (the same, mentioning GTA), hype (interest in GTA itself), reference.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: geo
    description: WORLD.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: dimension
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: signal_date
    description: UTC day.
    config:
      meta:
        dex:
          role: time
          null_rule: never
    data_tests:
    - not_null
  - name: signal_value
    description: Counts for posts and pageviews. Never add across signals or sources.

  - name: is_available

version: 2
models:
- name: fct_day_off_index
  description: 'The Day-Off Index: the average year-over-year change, in percent, of US Google searches for call in sick, sick day and day off work over the configured window. One row per window, always carrying its per-phrase breakdown.'
  config:
    meta:
      dex:
        grain:
          - index_window
        population:
          rule: One row for the configured window (vars day_off_index_*).
        assumptions:
          - decision: How the phrases combine
            chosen: plain average of the per-phrase percent changes
            evidence: request
            detail: 'user: the index is the average of these 3 searches; each phrase is on its own 0-100 scale, so changes are averaged, not interest values'
            column: day_off_index
          - decision: A phrase not yet available
            chosen: index NULL
            evidence: default
            detail: an average over fewer phrases would be a different index
            column: day_off_index
          - decision: Old index columns (study_year, release_day, per-source lifts, source counts)
            chosen: removed; the index is one row per window, no longer per study year
            evidence: request
            detail: 'user: scratch everything of the old Day-Off Index and redefine it'
            column: study_year
          - decision: Old index column release_day
            chosen: removed
            evidence: request
            detail: the Thursday-lift design is retired
            column: release_day
          - decision: Old index column sources_total
            chosen: removed
            evidence: request
            detail: the Thursday-lift design is retired
            column: sources_total
          - decision: Old index column sources_with_lift
            chosen: removed
            evidence: request
            detail: the Thursday-lift design is retired
            column: sources_with_lift
          - decision: Old index column google_trends_lift
            chosen: removed
            evidence: request
            detail: the Thursday-lift design is retired
            column: google_trends_lift
          - decision: Old index column bluesky_lift
            chosen: removed
            evidence: request
            detail: the Thursday-lift design is retired
            column: bluesky_lift
          - decision: Old index column reddit_lift
            chosen: removed
            evidence: request
            detail: the Thursday-lift design is retired
            column: reddit_lift
          - decision: Index grain
            chosen: one row per window (index_window), was per study year
            evidence: request
            detail: 'user: one YoY comparison over a configurable window'
            column: index_window
          - decision: Breakdown travels with the index
            chosen: breakdown column on the index row
            evidence: request
            detail: 'user: the index is always accompanied by its breakdown, never left to be discovered'
            column: breakdown
  columns:
    - name: index_window
      description: <current_start_week>/<current_end_week>.
      config:
        meta:
          dex:
            role: key
            null_rule: never
      data_tests:
        - unique
        - not_null
    - name: current_start_week
      description: Sunday of the first week of the current window.
      config:
        meta:
          dex:
            role: attribute
            null_rule: never
      data_tests:
        - not_null
    - name: current_end_week
      description: Sunday of the last week of the current window.
      config:
        meta:
          dex:
            role: attribute
            null_rule: never
      data_tests:
        - not_null
    - name: prior_start_week
      description: Sunday of the first comparison week (weeks_back earlier).
      config:
        meta:
          dex:
            role: attribute
            null_rule: never
      data_tests:
        - not_null
    - name: prior_end_week
      description: Sunday of the last comparison week.
      config:
        meta:
          dex:
            role: attribute
            null_rule: never
      data_tests:
        - not_null
    - name: weeks
      description: Weeks in each window.
      config:
        meta:
          dex:
            role: attribute
            null_rule: never
            unit: count
      data_tests:
        - not_null
    - name: batch_id
      description: The Trends pull the values come from.
      config:
        meta:
          dex:
            role: attribute
            null_rule: never
      data_tests:
        - not_null
    - name: phrase_count
      description: Phrases in the index.
      config:
        meta:
          dex:
            role: attribute
            null_rule: never
            unit: count
      data_tests:
        - not_null
    - name: phrases_available
      description: Phrases whose change is available.
      config:
        meta:
          dex:
            role: attribute
            null_rule: never
            unit: count
      data_tests:
        - not_null
    - name: day_off_index
      description: Average of the phrases' year-over-year changes, in percent (50 = searches up 50% on average). Always report with `breakdown`.
      config:
        meta:
          dex:
            role: measure
            null_rule: 'NULL unless every phrase''s change is available: unavailable, never zero'
            aggregation: max
            additivity: non_additive
            unit: percent
    - name: breakdown
      description: Every phrase's change, e.g. 'call in sick +40.4% · day off work +73.4% · sick day +36.4%'. Report it with the index, every time.
      config:
        meta:
          dex:
            role: attribute
            null_rule: never
      data_tests:
        - not_null

name: gta6_impact
version: 1.0.0
profile: gta6_impact
model-paths:
- models
test-paths:
- data_tests
models:
  gta6_impact:
    staging:
      +materialized: view
    intermediate:
      +materialized: view
    marts:
      +materialized: table
vars:
  day_off_index_span_start: '2025-11-01'
  day_off_index_span_end: '2026-11-15'
  day_off_index_batch: 20261116T185310
  day_off_index_start_week: '2026-11-01'
  day_off_index_end_week: '2026-11-08'
  day_off_index_weeks: 2
  day_off_index_weeks_back: 52

-- One row per search phrase per Google week (labelled by its Sunday), from one weekly
-- Trends request per phrase that spans both years, so 2025 and 2026 share one 0-100 scale.
-- Keeps the requests over the configured span (older daily per-year pulls have no span and
-- drop out), and the pinned batch (var day_off_index_batch) or else the newest per phrase.
{%- set batch = var('day_off_index_batch', none) %}
with source as (
    select *
    from {{ source('raw', 'trends_interest') }}
    where span_start = date '{{ var("day_off_index_span_start") }}'
        and span_end = date '{{ var("day_off_index_span_end") }}'
),

chosen as (
    select
        term,
        {% if batch %}'{{ batch }}'{% else %}max(batch_id){% endif %} as batch_id
    from source
    group by term
)

select
    source.request_id,
    source.batch_id,
    source.span_start,
    source.span_end,
    source.geo,
    source.term,
    source.day as week_start,
    cast(source.interest as integer) as interest,
    source.is_partial
from source
inner join chosen
    on source.term = chosen.term
    and source.batch_id = chosen.batch_id

-- The Day-Off Index breakdown: one row per search phrase, its average weekly search
-- interest over the current window and over the same weeks a year earlier, and the change.
-- The window is configurable (vars day_off_index_*): a start week and an end week, or a
-- start week and a number of weeks. Weeks are Google's, labelled by their Sunday.
{%- set start_week = var('day_off_index_start_week') %}
{%- set end_week = var('day_off_index_end_week', none) %}
{%- set weeks = var('day_off_index_weeks', 2) %}
{%- set weeks_back = var('day_off_index_weeks_back', 52) %}
with params as (
    select
        date '{{ start_week }}' as current_start_week,
        {% if end_week -%}
        date '{{ end_week }}'
        {%- else -%}
        cast(date '{{ start_week }}' + 7 * ({{ weeks }} - 1) as date)
        {%- endif %} as current_end_week
),

windows as (
    select
        current_start_week,
        current_end_week,
        cast(current_start_week - 7 * {{ weeks_back }} as date) as prior_start_week,
        cast(current_end_week - 7 * {{ weeks_back }} as date) as prior_end_week,
        cast((current_end_week - current_start_week) / 7 + 1 as integer) as weeks
    from params
),

phrases as (
    select distinct term, geo, batch_id, span_start, span_end
    from {{ ref('stg_trends__weekly') }}
),

per_phrase as (
    select
        phrases.term,
        phrases.geo,
        phrases.batch_id,
        phrases.span_start,
        phrases.span_end,
        windows.current_start_week,
        windows.current_end_week,
        windows.prior_start_week,
        windows.prior_end_week,
        windows.weeks,
        avg(weekly.interest) filter (
            where weekly.week_start between windows.current_start_week
                and windows.current_end_week and not weekly.is_partial
        ) as current_avg_interest,
        avg(weekly.interest) filter (
            where weekly.week_start between windows.prior_start_week
                and windows.prior_end_week and not weekly.is_partial
        ) as prior_avg_interest,
        count(weekly.week_start) filter (
            where weekly.week_start between windows.current_start_week
                and windows.current_end_week and not weekly.is_partial
        ) as current_weeks_found,
        count(weekly.week_start) filter (
            where weekly.week_start between windows.prior_start_week
                and windows.prior_end_week and not weekly.is_partial
        ) as prior_weeks_found
    from phrases
    cross join windows
    left join {{ ref('stg_trends__weekly') }} as weekly
        on phrases.term = weekly.term
    group by
        phrases.term,
        phrases.geo,
        phrases.batch_id,
        phrases.span_start,
        phrases.span_end,
        windows.current_start_week,
        windows.current_end_week,
        windows.prior_start_week,
        windows.prior_end_week,
        windows.weeks
)

select
    term,
    geo,
    batch_id,
    span_start,
    span_end,
    current_start_week,
    current_end_week,
    prior_start_week,
    prior_end_week,
    weeks,
    current_weeks_found,
    prior_weeks_found,
    current_avg_interest,
    prior_avg_interest,
    case
        when current_weeks_found = weeks
            and prior_weeks_found = weeks
            and prior_avg_interest > 0
            then 100 * (current_avg_interest / prior_avg_interest - 1)
    end as pct_change
from per_phrase

-- The Day-Off Index: the average of the three phrases' year-over-year changes, in percent,
-- one row per window. It always carries its breakdown: `breakdown` spells out every phrase's
-- change, so the index is never read without it.
with terms as (
    select
        *,
        cast(current_start_week as varchar) || '/' || cast(current_end_week as varchar)
            as index_window
    from {{ ref('fct_day_off_index_terms') }}
)

select
    index_window,
    min(current_start_week) as current_start_week,
    min(current_end_week) as current_end_week,
    min(prior_start_week) as prior_start_week,
    min(prior_end_week) as prior_end_week,
    min(weeks) as weeks,
    max(batch_id) as batch_id,
    count(*) as phrase_count,
    count(pct_change) as phrases_available,
    case when count(pct_change) = count(*) then avg(pct_change) end as day_off_index,
    string_agg(
        term || ' ' || coalesce(printf('%+.1f%%', pct_change), 'not yet available'),
        ' · ' order by term
    ) as breakdown
from terms
group by index_window

-- The Day-Off Index never travels without its breakdown: a row with an index has one.
select *
from {{ ref('fct_day_off_index') }}
where day_off_index is not null
    and (breakdown is null or phrases_available <> phrase_count)

-- Every signal as one daily value per (source, signal, geo, UTC day).
-- A value that could not be read is NULL with is_available = false: unavailable, never zero.
with bluesky as (
    select
        'bluesky' as source,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'posts:day_off_gta' else 'posts:day_off' end as signal,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'day_off_gta' else 'day_off_intent' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        hit_date as signal_date,
        case when bool_and(is_available) then cast(sum(hits_total) as double) end as signal_value,
        bool_and(is_available) as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_bluesky__daily_hits') }}
    group by gta_filter, hit_date
),

hacker_news as (
    select
        'hacker_news' as source,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'posts:day_off_gta' else 'posts:day_off' end as signal,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'day_off_gta' else 'day_off_intent' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        hit_date as signal_date,
        case when bool_and(is_available) then cast(sum(hits_total) as double) end as signal_value,
        bool_and(is_available) as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_hn__daily_hits') }}
    group by gta_filter, hit_date
),

wikipedia as (
    select
        'wikipedia' as source,
        'pageviews:' || lower(article) as signal,
        case when article = 'Grand_Theft_Auto_VI' then 'hype' else 'reference' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        view_date as signal_date,
        cast(views as double) as signal_value,
        true as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_wiki__pageviews') }}
)

select * from bluesky
union all
select * from hacker_news
union all
select * from wikipedia

-- One row per UTC day of the study window and its control year, with its place relative
-- to that year's release Thursday.
with spine as (
    select cast(range as date) as date_day
    from range(date '2025-10-01', date '2027-01-01', interval 1 day)
),

years as (
    select
        date_day,
        case when date_day >= date '2026-01-01' then 2026 else 2025 end as study_year
    from spine
),

anchored as (
    select
        date_day,
        study_year,
        case study_year when 2026 then date '2026-11-19' else date '2025-11-20' end as release_day
    from years
)

select
    date_day,
    study_year,
    release_day,
    cast(date_day - release_day as integer) as days_from_release,
    isodow(date_day) as iso_day_of_week,
    dayname(date_day) as day_name,
    study_year = 2026 and date_day = release_day as is_gta_release_day
from anchored

select
    md5(
        signals.source || '|' || signals.signal || '|' || signals.geo || '|'
        || cast(signals.signal_date as varchar)
    ) as signal_day_key,
    signals.source,
    signals.signal,
    signals.signal_family,
    signals.geo,
    signals.signal_date,
    signals.signal_value,
    signals.is_available,
    dates.study_year,
    dates.days_from_release,
    dates.iso_day_of_week
from {{ ref('int_signals__daily') }} as signals
inner join {{ ref('dim_date') }} as dates
    on signals.signal_date = dates.date_day

baseline_sources.models/marts/fct_thursday_lift.sql:
-- Release Thursday over the Thursday before, per signal and study year.
with pairs as (
    select
        source,
        signal,
        signal_family,
        geo,
        study_year,
        max(signal_value) filter (where comparison_role = 'baseline') as baseline_value,
        max(signal_value) filter (where comparison_role = 'release') as release_value,
        coalesce(bool_or(is_available) filter (where comparison_role = 'baseline'), false)
            as is_baseline_available,
        coalesce(bool_or(is_available) filter (where comparison_role = 'release'), false)
            as is_release_available
    from {{ ref('fct_signal_daily') }}
    where comparison_role is not null
    group by source, signal, signal_family, geo, study_year
)

select
    md5(source || '|' || signal || '|' || geo || '|' || cast(study_year as varchar))
        as thursday_lift_key,
    source,
    signal,
    signal_family,
    geo,
    study_year,
    case study_year when 2026 then date '2026-11-19' else date '2025-11-20' end as release_day,
    baseline_value,
    release_value,
    is_baseline_available,
    is_release_available,
    case
        when is_baseline_available and is_release_available and baseline_value > 0
            then release_value / baseline_value
    end as lift,
    signal_family = 'day_off_intent'
    and source in ('google_trends', 'bluesky', 'reddit')
    and (source <> 'google_trends' or baseline_value >= 5) as is_index_component
from pairs
baseline_sources.models/staging/stg_trends__interest.sql:
-- Each Trends request is scaled to its own 0-100, so values only compare inside one request.
-- The ingester asks for one term per request (so each term uses the full range) and pulls
-- every request several times in one batch, because Trends samples. request_id is
-- <group>-<geo>-<year>-<batch>-<pull>. We keep the newest batch per (term group, geo,
-- study year) and take the per-day median across its pulls. Older multi-term requests
-- (the 2026-11 'day_off' group) are dropped: their terms shared one scale.
with source as (
    select
        *,
        cast(split_part(request_id, '-', 3) as integer) as study_year,
        split_part(request_id, '-', 4) as batch_id
    from {{ source('raw', 'trends_interest') }}
),

single_term_requests as (
    select request_id
    from source
    group by request_id
    having count(distinct term) = 1
),

newest_batch as (
    select source.term_group, source.geo, source.study_year, max(source.batch_id) as batch_id
    from source
    inner join single_term_requests using (request_id)
    group by source.term_group, source.geo, source.study_year
)

select
    source.term_group || '-' || source.geo || '-' || cast(source.study_year as varchar)
        || '-' || source.batch_id as request_id,
    source.study_year,
    source.term_group,
    source.geo,
    source.term,
    source.day as interest_date,
    median(cast(source.interest as double)) as interest,
    count(distinct source.request_id) as pull_count,
    bool_or(source.is_partial) as is_partial
from source
inner join single_term_requests using (request_id)
inner join newest_batch
    on source.term_group = newest_batch.term_group
    and source.geo = newest_batch.geo
    and source.study_year = newest_batch.study_year
    and source.batch_id = newest_batch.batch_id
group by
    source.term_group,
    source.geo,
    source.study_year,
    source.batch_id,
    source.term,
    source.day
baseline_sources.models/marts/fct_day_off_index.sql:
-- The Day-Off Index: geometric mean of per-source lifts (each source the geometric mean of
-- its own component signals), x 100. 100 is a normal week.
with components as (
    select * from {{ ref('fct_thursday_lift') }}
    where is_index_component
),

by_source as (
    select
        study_year,
        source,
        count(*) as signals_total,
        count(lift) as signals_with_lift,
        case
            when count(lift) = count(*) then exp(avg(ln(greatest(lift, 0.01))))
        end as source_lift
    from components
    group by study_year, source
)

select
    study_year,
    case study_year when 2026 then date '2026-11-19' else date '2025-11-20' end as release_day,
    count(*) as sources_total,
    count(source_lift) as sources_with_lift,
    case
        when count(source_lift) = count(*) then 100 * exp(avg(ln(source_lift)))
    end as day_off_index,
    max(case when source = 'google_trends' then source_lift end) as google_trends_lift,
    max(case when source = 'bluesky' then source_lift end) as bluesky_lift,
    max(case when source = 'reddit' then source_lift end) as reddit_lift
from by_source
group by study_year
baseline_sources.models/intermediate/int_signals__daily.s:
-- Every signal as one daily value per (source, signal, geo, UTC day).
-- A value that could not be read is NULL with is_available = false: unavailable, never zero.
with trends as (
    select
        'google_trends' as source,
        'search:' || lower(term) as signal,
        case when term_group = 'hype' then 'hype' else 'day_off_intent' end as signal_family,
        geo,
        interest_date as signal_date,
        case when not is_partial then cast(interest as double) end as signal_value,
        not is_partial as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_trends__interest') }}
),

bluesky as (
    select
        'bluesky' as source,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'posts:day_off_gta' else 'posts:day_off' end as signal,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'day_off_gta' else 'day_off_intent' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        hit_date as signal_date,
        case when bool_and(is_available) then cast(sum(hits_total) as double) end as signal_value,
        bool_and(is_available) as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_bluesky__daily_hits') }}
    group by gta_filter, hit_date
),

hacker_news as (
    select
        'hacker_news' as source,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'posts:day_off_gta' else 'posts:day_off' end as signal,
        case gta_filter when 'gta' then 'day_off_gta' else 'day_off_intent' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        hit_date as signal_date,
        case when bool_and(is_available) then cast(sum(hits_total) as double) end as signal_value,
        bool_and(is_available) as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_hn__daily_hits') }}
    group by gta_filter, hit_date
),

wikipedia as (
    select
        'wikipedia' as source,
        'pageviews:' || lower(article) as signal,
        case when article = 'Grand_Theft_Auto_VI' then 'hype' else 'reference' end as signal_family,
        'WORLD' as geo,
        view_date as signal_date,
        cast(views as double) as signal_value,
        true as is_available
    from {{ ref('stg_wiki__pageviews') }}
)

select * from trends
union all
select * from bluesky
union all
select * from hacker_news
union all
select * from wikipedia
baseline_sources.models/marts/dim_date.sql:
-- One row per UTC day of the study window and its control year, with its place relative
-- to that year's release Thursday.
with spine as (
    select cast(range as date) as date_day
    from range(date '2025-10-01', date '2027-01-01', interval 1 day)
),

years as (
    select
        date_day,
        case when date_day >= date '2026-01-01' then 2026 else 2025 end as study_year
    from spine
),

anchored as (
    select
        date_day,
        study_year,
        case study_year when 2026 then date '2026-11-19' else date '2025-11-20' end as release_day
    from years
)

select
    date_day,
    study_year,
    release_day,
    cast(date_day - release_day as integer) as days_from_release,
    isodow(date_day) as iso_day_of_week,
    dayname(date_day) as day_name,
    case cast(date_day - release_day as integer)
        when 0 then 'release'
        when -7 then 'baseline'
    end as comparison_role,
    study_year = 2026 and date_day = release_day as is_gta_release_day
from anchored
baseline_sources.models/marts/fct_signal_daily.sql:
select
    md5(
        signals.source || '|' || signals.signal || '|' || signals.geo || '|'
        || cast(signals.signal_date as varchar)
    ) as signal_day_key,
    signals.source,
    signals.signal,
    signals.signal_family,
    signals.geo,
    signals.signal_date,
    signals.signal_value,
    signals.is_available,
    dates.study_year,
    dates.days_from_release,
    dates.iso_day_of_week,
    dates.comparison_role
from {{ ref('int_signals__daily') }} as signals
inner join {{ ref('dim_date') }} as dates
    on signals.signal_date = dates.date_day
